representation_notes: PENDING_AUDIT_B. Use action endomorphisms of the complex sl2 module; the three Chevalley brackets and common invariant subspaces encode its representation and irreducibility. lam remains an integer; l=lam.toNat and Idx l=Fin(l+1), with H003 justifying the identification. M is a Z-submodule of V (equivalently an additive subgroup). R is the subring of Q generated by fractions with p-prime denominators; T005 proves it is exactly Z_(p). MR is its span inside V; T006 constructs the tensor identification, not an assumed embedding. Jc is initially a span, and T009 proves its exact coordinate-set meaning. All tensor spaces are scalar-first: VK=K tensor_Z M is the canonical flip of the source M tensor_Z K. FirstChange/ScalarData record checked natural maps, not assumptions. IntegralOps records restrictions whose existence is proved, and baseChange gives the tensor-induced action. All result structures are witness records and their existence is a step obligation.

steps.statement: LR.Strings lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Induct on the nonnegative lowering exponent using the three commutators; the successor version of the raising formula includes the m=0 case.

steps.statement: (∀ i : LR.Idx lam.toNat, LR.e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧ LinearIndependent ℂ (fun i : LR.Idx lam.toNat => LR.e y v i.val)
steps.explanation: Iterate raising to show nonvanishing. Isolate each coefficient using the product of h minus the other complex weights; all differences are nonzero in characteristic zero.

steps.statement: (∃ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, lam.toNat < m → (y^m) v = 0)
steps.explanation: Use dimension to upgrade independence to a basis. The next lowering vector has an absent eigenvalue, hence is zero in that basis; further powers vanish.

steps.statement: LR.StringResult lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Derive the basic x,y,h actions, then iterate and divide by factorials to obtain both integral binomial formulas, including the zero branches. Package N001.

steps.statement: ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ LR.R p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ)
steps.explanation: Prove that fractions with p-prime denominators form a subring, so the closure definition of R has exactly the intended carrier. This is a checked representation bridge.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.LatticeEmbedding p lam.toNat M)
steps.explanation: The H006 basis is reindexed by Fin(l+1), equivalently the source reindexing by dimension. Base-change it to R. Complex independence proves injectivity of tensor multiplication and identifies its range with the R-span MR; obtain the displayed equivalence and complex spanning.

steps.statement: LR.Preserves p lam.toNat M x y h
steps.explanation: Restrict the divided powers to M and extend preservation to its R-span. Restrict h=[x,y]. Prime-to-p factorials and the binomial-factorial identity give all required units in R.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.LocalResult p lam.toNat M x y h B
steps.explanation: Compute the three matrix-unit identities on the characteristic-zero basis. Invert the binomial unit in R and compose to show every coordinate matrix unit preserves MR. Package N002, including the proved tensor embedding and integral restrictions.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Nonempty (LR.Decomposition p lam.toNat M v B)
steps.explanation: Prove the exact membership characterizations of the span-defined Jc objects. Matrix units identify all coordinate modules with J at e0=v. Projection of a finite basis gives finite generation; spanning gives nonzeroness. The coordinate sum defines the R-linear equivalence.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.RationalEmbedding p M v
steps.explanation: Construct multiplication Q tensor_R J to C by balancing. Put finitely many rational tensor factors over one nonzero integer denominator to prove injectivity. Base-change a finite generating family to prove finite dimensionality.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ d : LR.Decomposition p lam.toNat M v B, ∃ Phi : (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] LR.MR p M) ≃ₗ[ℚ] (LR.Idx lam.toNat → LR.T p M v), ∀ q c, Phi (q ⊗ₜ[LR.R p] d.coordEquiv c) = fun i => q ⊗ₜ[LR.R p] c i
steps.explanation: Rationalize the coordinate isomorphism. Define both maps by balanced tensor maps, with inverse the finite sum of the coordinate injections, and check their composites on elementary tensors.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Module.finrank ℚ (LR.T p M v) = 1
steps.explanation: The rationalized localized lattice has dimension n from its R-basis. The checked coordinate isomorphism gives dimension n*r on the other side. Finite dimensionality and n>0 imply r=1.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.CoordinateResult p lam.toNat M v B
steps.explanation: A nonzero a in J gives a nonzero rational tensor. Rank one makes it a rational basis; multiplication then expresses each c in J as a rational multiple of a. Package all of N003.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ ∃ g : Fin k → ℂ, (∀ j, g j ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ g j ≠ 0) ∧ LR.Jc p M v = Submodule.span (LR.R p) (Set.range g)
steps.explanation: Choose finite generators of the nonzero module J and delete zero entries. Reindex the remaining nonempty finite list.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ (k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → ℂ), 0 < k → (∀ j, g j ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ g j ≠ 0) → ∃ a : ℂ, a ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ nu : Fin k → ℤ, ∃ u : Fin k → (LR.R p)ˣ, (∀ j, g j = ((((p : ℚ) ^ nu j) * ((u j : LR.R p) : ℚ) : ℚ) : ℂ) * a) ∧ ∃ j0 : Fin k, ∀ j, nu j0 ≤ nu j
steps.explanation: Use the rational-line assertion, factor each nonzero rational coefficient as p to an integer power times a unit of R, and choose the minimum exponent. The valuation/unit factorization may use the rational p-adic valuation library directly.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.PrincipalResult p lam.toNat M v B
steps.explanation: The generator with minimum exponent gives b and J=Rb. The coordinate decomposition proves that b times every e_i is a basis. Repeat for any nonzero principal generator, as required by N004.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.FirstChange p K M)
steps.explanation: Construct rho by inverting p-prime denominators, and the natural scalar-first tensor associativity equivalence. Check its inverse and elementary tensor formula. The scalar-first convention is the canonical flip of the source convention.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.ScalarData p K M)
steps.explanation: Prove R/pR is ZMod p with its fraction formula. Give MR/pMR its canonical ZMod p module structure. Construct the second natural tensor equivalence by taking classes, with inverse independent of the lift because p acts as zero on K.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Nonempty (LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B)
steps.explanation: Choose a principal generator and its localized basis. Base-change along rho and transport back along A to beta. Coordinate reduction gives the ZMod p quotient basis. Compute the dimension and positive cardinality.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ rb : LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B, ∀ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, LR.ReducedAction K lam.toNat M x y h o rb.beta
steps.explanation: The natural scalar maps intertwine restrictions and tensor extensions, checked on elementary tensors. Transfer the characteristic-zero formulas to b e_i and then beta. Tensor extension preserves brackets and the integer identities r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r; the factorial images are nonzero.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ rb : LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B, ∀ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, LR.ReducedControl K lam.toNat M x y h o rb.beta
steps.explanation: Transfer the matrix-unit product identity to beta (or verify it there using the transferred formulas). A binomial unit stays nonzero. An x,y-stable K-subspace is stable under powers, scalar multiples, and all products appearing in that identity.

steps.statement: ∃ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B ∧ LR.ReductionResult p K lam.toNat M x y h v B
steps.explanation: Choose the string basis and package the scalar identifications, quotient and reduced bases, tensor-induced operators, all reduced formulas, and matrix-unit invariance. This realizes the complete N005 output.

steps.statement: ∀ beta : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) K (LR.VK K M), Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), W ≠ ⊥ → ∃ w : LR.VK K M, w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ j : LR.Idx lam.toNat, beta.repr w j ≠ 0
steps.explanation: Any such nonempty basis makes the space nonzero. In a nonzero subspace choose w≠0; injectivity of basis coordinates gives a nonzero coordinate.

steps.statement: ∀ beta : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) K (LR.VK K M), ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), (∀ i j, LR.Inv W (LR.MU beta i j)) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: In the nonzero branch, apply each coordinate matrix unit to w. Divide by its nonzero j-th coordinate to put every basis vector in W, so W is top.

steps.statement: Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∃ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), LR.Inv W (o.xz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.yz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.hz.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: Use the N005 reduced basis for nonzeroness, and its matrix-unit invariance with the independent matrix-unit subspace lemma. Universally quantify over W. The generators span L(K), including characteristic 2; the singleton l=0 case requires no special argument. This is P.
